subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw make `compaction` and `contextPruning` supported per-agent config surfaces, and what merge/fallback semantics must the active implementation use before merge?
rationale: This is a new strict config contract that affects session context, provider/model routing, auth-profile isolation, docs, and upgrade behavior; code inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Approve bounded per-agent overrides
options.body: Support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as additive overrides that deep-merge over defaults and are proven across schema, runtime, docs, and upgrade validation.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model only
options.body: Accept only the highest-impact `agents.list[].compaction.model` routing override now and leave broader pruning/compaction knobs for a later design.

options.title: Reject core config expansion
options.body: Keep context-management knobs global for now and ask users to separate deployments or wait for a broader configuration model.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded per-agent overrides
recommendation.body: Support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as additive overrides that deep-merge over defaults and are proven across schema, runtime, docs, and upgrade validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent adjacent work on agent config cleanup and compaction tests, and the decision is primarily about core config shape rather than a narrow line-level repair.
